en: The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Dharma Gate of the Letterless Treasury of Pervasive Illuminating Radiance, translated again by the Tripitaka Master Divākara of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was dwelling on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great [assembly].
The Bodhisattvas and the community of bhikṣus were present in a multitude of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas.

All those bodhisattvas had attained great wisdom and skillful means; they were all able to penetrate the treasury of the dharma that is without letters, possessed the eloquence of joyful speech that does not conflict with the ultimate and conventional truths, and were courageous and diligent, forever free from the hindrances and entanglements.
He has subdued his faculties and is free from attachment; he regards all sentient beings with compassion as if they were his only child;
he cherishes true wisdom as if it were a great island of jewels; he takes shame and remorse as his body and concentration and wisdom as his head;

he takes great kindness and compassion as his essential nature; he discerns the wholesome and the unwholesome, as well as the real and unreal dharmas, and clearly illuminates the two kinds of emptiness.
Abiding in the supreme and wondrous stage, he attains great renown and sleeps in eternal peace;
he practices with certainty the most sublime Dharma and forever leaves behind the inferior body of the womb.
Manifesting birth to protect the land, all his actions are universally virtuous; transcending the triple world, he is able to rescue those within it. His...
Their conduct was pure and they had thoroughly mastered the welfare of both themselves and others; all were fully endowed with such virtues.
Their names were:

Bodhisattva Victorious Reflection, Bodhisattva Victorious Course of Action, Bodhisattva Wondrous Sound, Bodhisattva Beautiful Sound, Bodhisattva Endowed with Eloquence, Bodhisattva Mass of Eloquence, Bodhisattva Jewel Topknot, Bodhisattva Thousand Spokes, Bodhisattva Dharma Rim, Bodhisattva Resonance of Dharma, Bodhisattva Lotus Face, Bodhisattva Lotus Eye, Bodhisattva Sustainer of the Earth, Bodhisattva Sustainer of the World, and Bodhisattva Voice Pervading the Great Earth.
All such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were of the appearance and likeness of youths; they served as the leaders within this assembly, each accompanied by their own retinue.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara was surrounded by an immeasurable and incalculable assembly of consecrated and enthroned bodhisattvas;
the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta was surrounded by an immeasurable billion-fold host of Great Brahmā deities;
and the Bodhisattva Viśeṣacintin was surrounded by an immeasurable number of bodhisattvas as well as Śakra, the Lord of Devas.
The Bodhisattva Gaganagañja was surrounded by an immeasurable host of Four Great Kings;
the Bodhisattva Viśvāmitra was surrounded by an immeasurable retinue of court ladies;

and the Bodhisattvas Samantabhadra, Vimatisamudghātin, Amoghadarśin, Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja of Immeasurable Skillful Means, Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, and others, each were surrounded by a great assembly of immeasurable bodhisattvas.
The Elder Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, and others were each surrounded by a multitude of great arhats;

even the sun and moon devaputras from all worlds throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, each came to the Buddha’s presence with their majestic radiance. Yet, through the Buddha’s spiritual power, their respective radiances could not shine forth, appearing like a mass of ink compared to Jambu-river gold.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable Nārāyaṇa devas, as well as Varuṇa, the Dragon King Takṣaka, the Dragon King Anavatapta, and others, each likewise surrounded by their retinues.
The Gandharva King Surūpa was also surrounded by an immeasurable host of gandharvas;
the Kinnara King Anāvilaya was surrounded by a retinue of seven hundred million kinnaras;

and so on, until all the bodhisattvas from worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions each invited their own Buddha and, together with their retinues, arrived here in this Sahā world. Having presented various supreme, wondrous, and supramundane offerings to the Buddhas and bodhisattvas, they each prostrated at the feet of the Buddhas and withdrew to stand to one side, sitting upon lotus thrones and gazing up at the World-Honored One.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Viśeṣacintin rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and spoke these words:
“World-Honored One!

For the sake of the fourfold assembly, I wish to inquire about the meaning of the two characters "Tathāgata. I only pray that the Tathāgata will explain them for me, so that we may all obtain benefit.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Victorious Reflection, saying: "Good son!
Does the Tathāgata appear in the world for the sake of only a single sentient being?"
He has appeared in the world for the benefit of immeasurable sentient beings. Good son!
You are now able, for the sake of the fourfold assembly, to inquire of me regarding the meaning of these two words.
"I shall explain it to you according to your questions.
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Viśeṣacintin, having received the Buddha’s permission, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
What dharmas are there that a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should eliminate and protect?
Furthermore, what dharmas are there that a Tathāgata realizes and fully awakens to?
"I pray that you will explain these two meanings.
At that time, the Buddha praised Victorious Reflection, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"

"Good son! You have already accomplished immeasurable merit and wisdom, and furthermore, you are empowered by the Tathāgata’s majestic spiritual power; thus you are able to ask me about such a meaning."
Listen attentively, listen attentively!
Reflect upon it well!
I shall analyze and explain it for you.
“Good son! There is one dharma that a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should eliminate.
What is this one dharma?
That which is called sensual desire.
Such a single dharma, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should eliminate. Good son!
Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva mahāsattva should eliminate.
What is this one dharma? It is anger.
In this way, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should eliminate.
Son of good family!
Furthermore, there is another dharma that a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should eliminate.
What is this one dharma? It is ignorance.
This one dharma is that which a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should eliminate.
"Good son! Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should eliminate.
What is this one dharma?
That which is called the grasping at a self—
this single dharma, son of good family, is what a bodhisattva mahāsattva should eliminate.
Son of good family!
Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should eliminate.
What is this one dharma?
It is called indolence.
In this way, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva mahāsattva should eliminate.
Son of good family!
Furthermore, there is another dharma that a bodhisattva mahāsattva should eliminate.
What is this one dharma?
It is sleep. This one dharma is what a bodhisattva mahāsattva should eliminate.
"Good son! Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should eliminate.
What is this one dharma?"
That which is called "defiled craving"—
this single dharma is what a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should eliminate. Good son!
Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva mahāsattva should eliminate.
What is this one dharma?
It is doubt and hesitation.
In this way, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva mahāsattva should eliminate.
Son of good family!
Furthermore, there is another dharma that a bodhisattva mahāsattva should eliminate.
What is this one dharma?
It is called ignorance.
This one dharma is that which a bodhisattva mahāsattva should eliminate.
"Good son! A bodhisattva mahāsattva should eliminate such dharmas as those described above. Good son!"
Regarding your question to me as to what further dharmas a bodhisattva mahāsattva should protect, I shall now explain them to you.
Noble son! There is one dharma that a bodhisattva mahāsattva should constantly protect.
What is this one dharma? It is:
"Do not exhort others to do what you yourself do not desire.
This is the one dharma that a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should always guard and protect.
Why is this? If a bodhisattva mahāsattva protects this Dharma, they are protecting the entire treasury of precepts of all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas.

Just as with all bodhisattvas: those who cherish their own lives should not kill; those who cherish their own wealth should not steal; those who cherish their own wives should not violate others; those who cherish truthful speech should not deceive others; those who cherish harmony should not cause division among others; those who cherish uprightness should not speak with crookedness or frivolity; those who cherish gentleness should not utter harsh abuse; those who cherish contentment should never give rise to covetousness toward others; those who cherish benevolence and forbearance should never give rise to anger toward others; and those who cherish right view should never instruct others to give rise to wrong views.

"Good son! When a bodhisattva thus resolves and declares, 'I now respectfully comply with the Tathāgata’s true teaching and shall diligently protect this Dharma with a devoted mind,' this is called the bodhisattva-mahāsattva's protection of one dharma."
"Good son! I see that all these bodhisattvas who seek unsurpassed great bodhi do so entirely for the sake of happiness; there is none among them who seeks it for the sake of suffering."
"Good son! For this reason, I say: 'What you do not desire for yourself, do not encourage others to do.
Such dharmas as these, a bodhisattva-mahāsattva should guard and protect."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Victorious Reflection again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
What dharmas have the Tathāgata realized and awakened to?"
“I only pray that you will expound its meaning for me.
The Buddha said, “Good son!
There is not a single dharma that is awakened to or realized by the Tathāgata.
Why is this? Because within all dharmas there is neither awakening nor realization; this is what is realized and awakened to by the Tathāgata.
"Good son! All dharmas are fundamentally without any dharma; this is what the Tathāgata has awakened to and realized.
All dharmas are fundamentally without any cessation; this is what the Tathāgata has awakened to and realized."
The Tathāgata has awakened to and realized that the nature of all dharmas is free from the two extremes;
the Tathāgata has awakened to and realized that all dharmas are fundamentally without reality.
Furthermore, son of good family!
All phenomena arise solely through the power of the causes and conditions of one's own karma;
yet these causes and conditions do not abide for even a single moment, being like flashes of lightning—it is such karmic conditions that the Tathāgata has awakened to and realized.

Therefore, I say that all phenomena arise by way of causes and conditions, and all phenomena cease by way of causes and conditions; if one were apart from causes and conditions, there would be no karmic retribution.
The Tathāgata awakens to and knows such matters as these.
Son of good family!
This nature of all dharmas thus awakened to is called the Treasury of Pervasive Radiant Light.
"Good son! For what reason is the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) called a 'treasury' (garbha)?
It is because all the mundane and supramundane wisdom of sentient beings arises in dependence upon this treasury."
Just as one contemplates that dharma-nature with true wisdom, because wisdom arises in dependence upon it, it is called a "treasury" (*garbha*).

Furthermore, son of good family, I also declare that all dharmas are like an illusion, like a mirage, like the moon reflected in water; such matters as these have been realized and awakened to by the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, son of good family!
The nature and characteristics of all dharmas are a single flavor of liberation; such matters as these have been realized and awakened to by the Tathāgata.
Son of good family!
This liberation, the single flavor of the dharma-nature, is called the Treasury of Pervasive Radiant Light.
"Furthermore, good son, there is another dharma realized by the Tathāgata."
What is this one dharma?
It is that all dharmas are neither arising nor ceasing, neither increasing nor decreasing, neither coming nor going, neither grasping nor relinquishing, and neither caused nor conditioned.
The Tathāgata has awakened to and realized such dharmas as these.
Furthermore, son of good family, the Tathāgata thoroughly knows that all dharmas are devoid of intrinsic nature; they cannot be illustrated by analogy, nor can they be expressed through words.
Such dharmas as these have been awakened to and realized by the Tathāgata. Good son!
All such dharmas as those described above are entirely what the Tathāgata has awakened to and realized.
When the Buddha spoke this Dharma of the Wordless Treasury of Pervasive Illuminating Radiance, bodhisattvas as numerous as atoms attained the ten stages;
furthermore, immeasurable bodhisattvas dwelt in the various stages;
and yet more immeasurable bodhisattvas realized hundreds of thousands of great samādhis.
Furthermore, there were sentient beings as numerous as the atoms of immeasurable worlds who resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who attained the fruit of *arhatship*;

and there were immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who were liberated from the various sufferings of the hells, hungry ghosts, and animals, being reborn among humans and devas to enjoy supreme and wondrous bliss.
All those in the assembly shall not have come in vain; there is not a single person who passes through this in emptiness.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Rāhula, saying:
"O son of good family!..."
"You should receive and uphold this essential teaching of mine.
At that time, ninety billion bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the assembly, having heard these words, empowered by the Buddha's spiritual authority, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

We vow that in the future time and final age within this Sahā world, whenever we see those capable of being vessels for the Dharma, we shall proclaim this sutra for them; we pray only that the World-Honored One need not worry on this account.
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

If in future ages there are good men or good women who are able to receive, uphold, and recite this sutra, we shall provide them with protection and ensure that all their aspirations and requests are fulfilled."
"Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family are able to uphold this sutra; they are vessels of the Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One, seeing that the nine billion bodhisattvas and the four heavenly kings had made such requests, spoke these words:
“Good son! This Dharma-gate of the Treasury of Pervasive Illuminating Radiance Without Letters, which I have never previously expounded since attaining Buddhahood, I now proclaim for your sake.”
"Good son! Those sentient beings of future ages who shall hear this rare Dharma-gate should know that they have long since accomplished immeasurable merit and wisdom;
one should know that such persons are thereby serving and making offerings to me."
One should know that such a person carries upon their shoulders the great Bodhi of the Buddha;
one should know that such a person will certainly attain the accomplishment of eloquence;
one should know that such a person will certainly attain a pure Buddha-field.
You should know that when such a person approaches the end of life, they will certainly behold Amitābha Buddha surrounded by a great assembly of bodhisattvas;
you should know that such a person will constantly see my own body on Vulture Peak Mountain, as well as this multitude of bodhisattvas;
you should know that such a person has already attained the inexhaustible treasury of the Dharma.
"You should know that this person attains the knowledge of past lives;
you should know that this person does not fall into the evil realms.
Furthermore, good son!"

Now I shall speak of this unprecedented Dharma: if in future ages there are good men or good women who, even if they have already committed the five heinous crimes or other such offenses, hear this Dharma-gate and are able to write it down, uphold it, read and recite it, explain it, or encourage others to write it down, uphold it, read and recite it, and explain it—I see that such persons shall not fall into the evil realms. All their affliction-obstructions (*kleśāvaraṇa*), karma-obstructions (*karmāvaraṇa*), and retribution-obstructions (*vipākāvaraṇa*) shall become purified. In future lives, such persons will fully attain the five eyes; they will be consecrated by all Buddhas together; they will be protected and remembered by all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, and Bodhisattvas; and in whatever place they are born in future lives, they will possess all faculties complete and without deficiency.

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vimati-vinodana and the others, along with the bhikṣus, the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of supernatural beings, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Dharma Gate of the Wordless Treasury of Pervasive Illuminating Radiance.
